source.title: Fractal Structure and Generalization Properties of Stochastic Optimization Algorithms
source.authors: A. Camuto; George Deligiannidis; Murat A. Erdogdu; M. Gürbüzbalaban; Umut Simsekli; Lingjiong Zhu

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures a different optimization-derived complexity quantity and reports its association with the training–test gap; it does not test the specific interventions or sharpness measure named in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports correlations between its estimated complexity R and the generalization error, plus a trend of R with step size. Cited findings from other studies and theoretical bounds without measured outcomes are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests an invariant-measure complexity proxy, not any listed claim version. Its Jacobian-based quantity is not magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness (V7). Using convolutional and fully connected models and varying batch size does not establish the comparisons required by V3 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct about the conditional, asymptotic generalization bound and supporting complexity–gap correlations. Correct its caveat: the cross-entropy inconclusiveness follows the R–step-size analysis, rather than being explicitly reported for the R–generalization-gap association. The authors also identify reliance on invariant measures and asymptotic analysis as a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an invariant-measure and Jacobian-norm framework to study generalization; it does not apply the interventions or measurement recipes in the listed original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported R–generalization-error relationship is inconclusive for classification models trained with cross-entropy loss. R decreases with increasing step size in the reported BHP experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated inverse average log-Jacobian norm R correlates positively with the absolute training–test loss gap; all reported architecture plots have one-sided p-values below 0.001.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An optimization-derived Jacobian complexity proxy tracks the generalization gap in the tested SGD settings.

fits_no_version.finding: R decreases with increasing step size for the two-hidden-layer BHP network. The corresponding trend is inconclusive for classification models trained with cross-entropy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relationship between step size and estimated invariant-measure complexity depends on the tested task or loss.

record.problems: The paper states that results were inconclusive for classification models trained with cross-entropy loss. The experiments rely on estimated invariant-measure quantities and do not report individual numerical correlation values in the supplied prose.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows identified. Theoretical bounds and claims about batch size or step size without a measured generalization outcome, and results cited from other work, were left out.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width required to fit training data.
Comparative image-classification test error and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under different tuning recipes.
Large-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Effects of dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The states indicate that these measures cannot determine any listed version; they do not deny the reported proxy correlations. No version-specific missing result is identifiable from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.

rows.subject: VGG11 and FCNs (aggregate as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Estimated R, the inverse of an average log-Jacobian norm, and compared it with the generalization error across the reported model architectures.

conditions.value: CIFAR10, SVHN and Boston House Prices (BHP)

rows.measure: Association between estimated R and generalization error (|training loss − test loss|).
rows.value: R and generalization error are positively correlated; one-sided p-value is significantly less than 0.001 for all model architectures.
rows.uncertainty: One-sided p-value significantly less than 0.001; 95% confidence interval shading is shown for the fitted regression in Figure 3.
rows.note: The text describes the result across a variety of convolutional and fully connected architectures; individual plotted values are not stated in the prose.
rows.check: The positive R–loss-gap association is reported, but cannot establish any listed version. The subject description omits VGG16, which Appendix F includes among the experimental architectures. The subsequent cross-entropy caveat concerns the R–step-size trend; it should not be attached to this correlation as an established limitation.

rows.subject: 2 layer FCN
rows.operation_detail: Plotted estimated R against step size η.
rows.measure: Estimated R as a function of η.
rows.note: The text reports the direction of the trend but gives no numerical values.
rows.check: The decreasing R–step-size trend is reported for BHP, but measures neither held-out performance nor magnitude-aware sharpness. Appendix F defines BHP training as 100000 steps rather than a measured convergence criterion.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
